 Justice S.K. Sahoo

This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
This is an application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.
Heard.

The appellant-petitioner has been convicted under sections 323/354-B/376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and sections 4/10 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of twenty years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- (rupees ten // 2 // thousand), in default of payment of fine, to undergo further R.I. for a period of six months for the offence under section 376(3) of the Indian Penal Code and R.I. for a period of six months for the offence under section 323 of the Indian Penal Code and no separate punishment is awarded under section 354-B of the Indian Penal Code and sections 4/10 of the POCSO Act in view of section 42 of the POCSO Act and both the substantive Sunil @ Samir Sahu vs State Of Odisha And on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90377947/
1 sentences were directed to run concurrently by the learned Additional Sessions Judge -cum- Children's Court, Sonepur in Special G.R. Case No.12 of 2020.
On 15.02.2024, when submission was made by the learned counsel for the appellant/petitioner so also the respondent no.2 that the petitioner and the victim i.e. daughter of respondent no.2 have already got married and the marriage certificate has been issued, learned counsel for the State was asked to obtain instruction in respect of authenticity of the marriage certificate.
Today, learned counsel for the State has produced the written instruction received from the Inspector in-charge of Birmaharajpur (I/c) police station dated 11.03.2024, which indicates that the petitioner has married to the daughter of the respondent no.2.

entities.text: Sunil @ Samir Sahu vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The written report is taken on record.

In view of the development made in the // 3 // meantime and since there is no chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future as it is an appeal of the year 2023, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.

Let the appellant-petitioner be released on bail pending disposal of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
Accordingly, the I.A. is disposed of.
There shall be stay of realization of fine amount imposed by the learned trial Court on the appellant- petitioner till disposal of the criminal appeal.
Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge RKM Signed by: RABINDRA KUMAR MISHRA
